description: Typed extraction of obligations and asserted requirements for P7 run 1. The extractor fills these fields from the given documents only. The comparator (comparator.py) reads them; the extractor never sees the comparator's rules.

statuses.binding: The text plainly requires this value.
statuses.selected_realization: The text describes this value as a chosen way of doing the work, revisable by its author, not as a requirement.
statuses.unspecified: The text says nothing about this property.
statuses.ambiguous: The text supports more than one reading. Do not resolve it; record the readings in 'readings'.

initiator.meaning: Who must start or issue the action.
initiator.comparison: A larger set permits more actors and is weaker.

outcome_owner.meaning: Who or what must bring about the outcome.
outcome_owner.comparison: A larger set permits more actors and is weaker.

verifier.meaning: Who must establish that the outcome holds.
verifier.comparison: A larger set permits more actors and is weaker.

path_fact.meaning: Required facts about how or by which route the outcome is produced.
path_fact.comparison: A larger set requires more and is stronger.

acceptance_evidence.comparison: A larger set requires more and is stronger.

actor_notes.any: No restriction on who. Use only when the text plainly permits anyone.
actor_notes.component: Generic: the single component the obligation is about, when no other actor token fits (used by fixtures).

item_notes.other: Something not in the list. Put the quoted span in 'other_text'. The comparator cannot compare 'other' and reports it as not established.

entry.id: string, unique in the output, e.g. 'F-043#1'
entry.role: 'parent' (a source of requirements) or 'derived' (a later document asserting requirements)
entry.span: exact quoted text the entry is extracted from

<property>.value: list of actor tokens or item tokens; empty when status is unspecified
<property>.readings: for ambiguous only: list of alternative value lists

entry.asserted_as: derived entries only: 'inherited' (presented as already required by a parent), 'proposed' (offered as a new requirement for someone to decide), 'new' (imposed as binding without citing a parent), 'realization_choice' (the author's own revisable choice), 'unchanged' (presented as unchanged from a parent)
entry.cites: derived entries only: {'kind': 'specific', 'parent_entry': '<id>'} or {'kind': 'general', 'text': '<quoted citation>'} or {'kind': 'none'}
entry.replaces_parent: derived entries only: true if the entry presents itself as the complete requirement replacing the cited parent's
